summary: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship funds young African leaders for a one-year Honours or a two-year Master's degree at any recognised South African university, in any field. It covers tuition, accommodation and meals, medical aid, study materials, a personal allowance and economy travel, plus a compulsory leadership development programme. It is won by academically strong applicants who show the Foundation's four principles: leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship.
lookfor: Leadership with moral authority — inspiring others and serving human rights and dignity
Reconciliation — valuing diversity, openness and willingness to reflect on yourself
Education — academic excellence (above 70% or an upper-second degree) plus character
Entrepreneurship — initiative and creativity that improves society and Africa's position
Readiness for personal growth and full commitment to the leadership programme
cycle: Applications for the 2027 scholarship closed on 14 April 2026. Applications for 2028 open on 9 March 2027 (official); the window has recently closed in mid-April. Last cycle: shortlist rounds mid- and late July, interview decisions end of August, final awards end of October. Check the official page for 2028 dates.

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen of an African country?
eligibility.no: Only African citizens can apply. Consider Chevening or Commonwealth awards.

eligibility.q: Will you be between 19 and 29 in the year you apply (and under 30 when you take up the scholarship)?
eligibility.no: If you are 30 or older, look at the Mastercard Foundation programmes (many allow up to 35) or the Joint Japan/World Bank scholarship.

eligibility.q: Will you hold an undergraduate degree with excellent results (above 70% or upper-second class) by 1 January of the scholarship year?
eligibility.no: Final-year students can apply if they will graduate in time. If your grades are below this, look at other awards.

eligibility.q: Can you study at postgraduate level in English?
eligibility.no: Improve your academic English first; the Foundation points applicants to a free English test at englishradar.com.

eligibility.q: Will you study full-time in South Africa for an Honours or Master's degree and attend every leadership workshop?
eligibility.no: Attendance is compulsory and you may work at most 12 hours a week. If you cannot commit, this award is not a fit.

eligibility.q: Can you get admission to a South African university by January of the scholarship year?
eligibility.no: You must secure your own place. Start university applications alongside the scholarship.

steps.title: Check eligibility and the programme commitments
steps.why: The age, grade and attendance rules are strict. Knowing them early saves wasted effort.
do: Open the official 'Apply' page and read Steps 1–3 and the FAQs.
Check your age against the 19–29 rule for the year you apply.
Check your grade: above 70% or upper-second class (2:1).
Read the terms and conditions PDF: compulsory workshops (three in year one, two in year two), full-time study, maximum 12 hours paid work a week, no other scholarships at the same time.
Decide on Honours (1 year) or Master's (2 years).
tips: The scholarship cannot be deferred to a later year, so apply for the year you can actually start.
avoid: Planning to keep a full-time job while studying.
check: I meet every must-have rule and accept the commitments.

steps.title: Study the four principles
steps.why: Selection is built on leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship. One essay is about the principles.
do: Download and read the MRF guiding principles PDF.
For each principle, write two real examples from your life.
Mark your weakest principle and think about honest reflection you can show there.
Keep this page; you will use it for essays and interviews.
tips: Reconciliation is the principle most applicants ignore; think about times you bridged divides or changed your own view.
avoid: Treating 'leadership' as only holding a title.
check: I have two examples for each principle.

steps.title: Build your timeline for the 2028 round
steps.why: The application window is short (about five weeks). Referees and documents need longer than that.
do: Put 9 March 2027 (applications open) in your calendar.
Expect the window to close in mid-April 2027 (last round: 14 April). Confirm the date when the portal opens.
Set targets: referees asked by end of January, documents ready by end of February, essays drafted by 9 March, submit by 1 April.
Add the selection months: July (shortlists), end of August (interview invitations), October (final results).
tips: Draft essays before the portal opens so you can apply early.
check: All dates are in my calendar with reminders.

steps.title: Choose your South African university and programme
steps.why: The scholarship is only awarded if you get admission to a South African institution. A clear programme choice also strengthens your essays.
do: List Honours or Master's programmes in your field at 3–4 South African universities.
Note each one's entry rules, application deadline and fees.
Check whether your foreign degree needs SAQA evaluation (foreign qualifications).
Plan to apply to the universities in parallel with the scholarship.
tips: Choose programmes that fit a clear story about what you want to do in Africa.
avoid: Waiting for the scholarship result before applying to universities.
check: I have 2–3 programmes and know their deadlines.

steps.title: Gather ID, degree certificate and transcripts
steps.why: The application needs a passport (or ID), degree certificate and academic transcripts, all in English.
do: Check your passport is valid; renew it now if it expires within two years (Nigeria: NIS e-passport portal).
Request official transcripts from your university's Exams and Records office.
Scan your degree certificate; final-year students prepare their latest results and a letter confirming expected graduation.
Name files clearly (Surname_Transcript.pdf).
tips: If you do not have a passport yet, the Foundation's FAQ says to discuss passport problems with them.
check: All documents are scanned and readable.

steps.title: Start SAQA verification if you studied outside South Africa
steps.why: International applicants may need SAQA evaluation of their degree. It can take 4–8 weeks and the Foundation does not pay for it.
do: Ask your target South African university whether it needs a SAQA evaluation of your degree.
If yes, open the SAQA website and follow 'Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications'.
Prepare certified copies and pay the fee as instructed.
Save the reference number.
tips: Start early so it does not delay your university admission.
avoid: Assuming the scholarship covers SAQA or university application fees — it does not.
check: I know whether I need SAQA and have started if so.

steps.title: Write the personal journey essay
steps.why: This essay shows who you are, what shaped you and how you have grown — the core of 'readiness for personal growth'.
do: Pick 2–3 turning points in your life (a challenge, a choice, a change of mind).
For each, say what happened, what you did and what you learned about yourself.
Connect your journey to where you want to go and why South Africa now.
Keep within the word limit shown in the portal.
tips: Honest reflection beats a list of achievements.
check: The essay shows growth, not just success.

links.t: Watch: How I Won Mandela Rhodes Scholarship (and Insider Tips for YOU) (GN Inspire Podcast)

steps.prompt: A short essay on your personal journey.
steps.limit: Check the current guidance (shown in the portal)

steps.title: Write the principles essay
steps.why: The second essay answers a specific question about the Foundation's principles. It tests whether your values match theirs.
do: Read the question in the portal carefully when it opens.
Choose the principle(s) the question targets and use your examples from the principles step.
Structure: your position, one strong example, what it taught you, how you will act on it as a scholar.
Ask someone to check it answers the exact question.
tips: Engage with the idea (e.g. reconciliation with reparation) rather than only praising Mandela.
avoid: Quotes and slogans instead of your own thinking.
check: My essay answers the exact question with a personal example.
steps.prompt: A short essay on a specific question about the Foundation's principles (set each year).
steps.limit: Check the current guidance (shown in the portal)

steps.title: Brief three referees
steps.why: Three recommendation letters are required. In past rounds, referees logged in to the platform and uploaded letters directly.
do: Choose three people who know your character and work: e.g. a lecturer, a supervisor, and a community leader.
Ask them by the end of January; send your CV, draft essays and a note on the four principles.
When the portal opens, enter their details so they receive the upload link.
Follow up a week before the deadline.
tips: Ask each referee to cover a different side of you (academic, leadership, service).
avoid: Referees who do not know you well.
check: Three referees have agreed and have my documents.

links.t: UP: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship 2022 call (past requirements, PDF)

steps.title: Complete and submit the online application
do: Open the application platform from the Apply page when it opens on 9 March 2027.
Fill in personal details exactly as on your passport.
Paste in your two essays and upload documents.
Check your referees' letters are uploaded.
Submit and save the confirmation.
avoid: Waiting until the last night when the platform is busy.
check: I have a submission confirmation and all three letters are in.

links.t: Watch: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship 2027 (Fully Funded) | How to Apply + Eligibility for Africans (GN Inspire Podcast)

steps.title: Apply to your South African universities
steps.why: You must have admission by January of the scholarship year; the scholarship does not arrange it for you.
do: Apply online to your chosen programmes.
Pay application fees (not covered by the Foundation).
Upload transcripts, degree certificate and SAQA evaluation if needed.
Track each application status.
tips: Apply to more than one university to be safe.
avoid: Missing university deadlines while waiting for scholarship news.

links.t: Apply page (studies and university acceptance FAQ)

steps.title: Get through the shortlisting rounds
steps.why: Last cycle had shortlist notices in mid-July and late July, then interview decisions at the end of August.
do: Check your email (and spam) weekly from July.
Reply quickly to any request for more information.
Keep your referees updated.
tips: Use this time to keep building your university admission.
avoid: Missing an email because it went to spam.

steps.title: Prepare for the interview
steps.why: Interviews test your values and self-awareness against the four principles.
do: Reread your essays and the principles PDF.
Prepare examples for each principle and one honest weakness you are working on.
Practise discussing current issues in Africa and South Africa.
Do a mock interview with a mentor.
tips: Show you can listen and change your mind — reconciliation in action.
avoid: Rehearsed, polished answers that hide who you are.
check: I can discuss each principle with a personal example.

links.t: Watch: Preparing For Your MRF Interview (The Mandela Rhodes Foundation)

steps.title: Accept, secure admission and get your study visa
steps.why: Awards are announced around the end of October. From October to December you must confirm your university place and get a South African study visa.
do: Accept the award as instructed.
Confirm your university admission and send it to the Foundation.
Apply for a South African study visa (the Foundation provides visa assistance).
Note the workshop dates and plan travel.
tips: Ask the Foundation early for the visa support letter.
avoid: Booking travel before the visa is approved.
check: I have accepted, secured admission and applied for my visa.

faq.a: No. The scholarship funds one-year Honours or two-year Master's degrees.

faq.q: Can I study at any South African university?
faq.a: Yes, any recognised South African higher education institution, in any field.

faq.q: Does it cover university application or SAQA fees?
Can I work while on the scholarship?
faq.a: Up to 12 hours a week of paid work.

faq.q: Is it the same as the Rhodes Scholarship to Oxford?
faq.a: No. Mandela Rhodes is for study in South Africa and is run by the Mandela Rhodes Foundation.
